what_it_does: XaaS (Acceleration as a Service) Containers solve a portability versus performance trade-off in supercomputing. Traditional containers package code and binaries, but this forces performance-tuning decisions early for one specific hardware setup, then lose those optimizations when the container runs on different machines. XaaS Containers instead package code in two forms: human-readable source code and Intermediate Representation (IR—a hardware-neutral middle layer). When deployed, the system can make hardware-specific optimizations at installation time for the actual target machine. The system also uses large language models to automatically discover what optimizations will help and builds hardware-tailored binaries without manual tuning.
